\caption{Fidelity of simulated belief updates by model size, grouped by family and ordered by active parameters. $\Delta$ is the mean paired difference in final stance (human $-$ model); MAE is its absolute counterpart and is what the models are ranked on. Both are on the normalised 5-point scale, over 970 persona-topic cases from 389 participants on which every model produced a parseable response. \textit{Size} gives active parameters per token, with stored parameters after a slash where the two differ: for the mixture-of-experts models because most experts are idle, and for Gemma's \mbox{E-}named models because per-layer embeddings are not resident on the accelerator. \textit{Valid} is the share of all 1173 cases that model parsed and $n_{\mathrm{tries}}{=}3$ the share that needed every one of its 3 allowed attempts; both are over all cases, before the complete-case intersection above was taken, so a low figure means that row rests on a subset the model selected by succeeding on it. Each 95\% CI is a cluster bootstrap percentile interval for the statistic beside it: the 389 participants are resampled with replacement, each carrying all of their topics, the statistic is recomputed on every resampled dataset, and the bounds are the $2.5$th and $97.5$th percentiles of those 10{,}000 values. $p$ tests $\Delta = 0$ by a two-sided paired sign-flip permutation test over 1{,}000{,}000 resamples; it is the test of the paired signed difference, so it belongs with $\Delta$ and not with the MAE. $p$ is reported uncorrected; values in bold are significant at $\alpha = 0.05$ after Bonferroni correction across the 12 models ($p < 0.05/12$).}
